name: When do I need to hire a general contractor instead of managing an addition myself?

mainEntity.name: When do I need to hire a general contractor instead of managing an addition myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a general contractor whenever an addition involves structural framing, exterior tie-ins, and multiple specialized trades. While an architect or draftsman produces drawings, a general contractor manages the physical execution, coordinates foundation pours, and schedules licensed sub-trades for electrical and plumbing. Working with an owner-operated contractor like Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling provides a single point of contact on site, ensuring that framing, insulation, drywall, tile, and finish carpentry align directly with the engineered plans and inspection schedules.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hire a general contractor when projects require structural framing, foundation work, and multi-trade coordination to ensure code compliance and quality control.
